unit_result_entry.title: Balance zero-sensitive shift error against finite-sum truncation

spontaneous.spontaneous_reading: The quantitative proof is an error-budget argument in transform space. One term measures finite Dirichlet-sum truncation, the other measures the effect of shifting zeta away from the critical line; splitting according to distance from zeros and then balancing δ and ε creates the one-third norm rate.

directed.source_grounded_mathematics: Plancherel bounds the squared H-error by two transform-side integrals: a finite Möbius Dirichlet-polynomial discrepancy from 1/ζ(z+ε), and the shift discrepancy ζ(z)/ζ(z+ε)−1. Away from zeros the logarithmic derivative gives ε/δ control; near zeros a Burnol estimate is used. Their integrated contribution is O(ε²/δ²+δ), optimized at δ=ε^(2/3). A cutoff-sensitive Balazard–Saias estimate controls the first integral, giving an overall squared-error bound of order n^(−2ε/3)+ε^(2/3); choosing ε proportional to 1/log log n yields the proposition's norm rate.
directed.conceptual_reading: The proof decomposes by failure mode and tunes two thresholds. δ separates zero-near instability from the regular region, while ε balances analytic shift error against truncation decay.
directed.representation_or_bridge: Fourier–Mellin/Plancherel is the bridge from H-distance to zeta integrals. The intermediate objects are the shifted zeta ratio, the truncated reciprocal-zeta approximation, and the zero-distance partition.
directed.boundary_or_failure: This is explicitly a sketch under RH. A failed bound in either the zero-near region or the cutoff term would break the balance, and the argument does not supply an unconditional approximation rate.
directed.uncertainty: The prose supports the decomposition, scales, and choices, but the integral displays and cutoff-sensitive estimate are materially layout-damaged; exact integrands, constants, and normalized exponents require scan verification.
